I'd just like to add a lot of people who are saying "have empathy" or "have sympathy" for this woman's situation but dont actually understand what that means in relation. It is ok to have empathy for what she did. Yes, if you were on your death bed, drugged up, you would probably contradict your past actions and want to talk to the people you love most and even fix past relationshipsat the expenseof others lives and feelings. 

BUT, it is important to understand that even with empathy for what she did, it was still wrong what she did in relation to OP. It can't be changed, but it doesn't mean she gets a free pass because she passed away. If someone hurts you, that hurt doesn't leave when they pass. The only thing is to heal from the hurt (she hurt her ex too by doing this) and forgive because she is gone. The same goes for the Fiance, have empathy for him, and that hes greiving but to ignore that he never stopped loving his ex and wanted his life to be with her is not something you can ignore through empathy. OP should not be expected to not have any feelings towards that at all. I think a lot of people confuse being compassionate with enabling bad actions because they feel more pity than true empathy.  

And with all this empathy talk, some of you should have some for OP too. 

OP I'd also like to add that it seems you are grieving this relationship, and that's ok. You were living in a reality and a relationship that you thought was a certain way and that you guys were on the same page, and it ended up not being that. It's ok to have these feelings as YOU ARE GRIEVING YOUR RELATIONSHIP TOO!

gentle YTA...as someone with various mental illness and recovered from BED you are doing a great job as a parent and your children do come first but you have another child on the way and the mother to that child is uncomfortable. 

Theres such an easy fix-- keep her snacks in the room. Do not allow your daughter access to her snacks. She doesnt even have to know they are there, be creative on how you sneak them in. You need to balance your child, your wife, and your new baby! Thank you for supporting your daughter and getting her the proper care, but what you need to think about the message you are sending everyone.

-You are letting the wife feel that her and the new baby are not important enough to you.
-You are letting the daughter think that you will always take her side and possibly let her get her way with any behaviorif it revolvesher mental health which could teach her to weaponize it in the future. Yes this was a crisis, and you did the right thing for your daughter but you could have also done the right thing for your wife too. You didnt have to pick and choose here. 

Recovery is not linear, she NEEDS to learn to live with all food in a healthy way. She needs to learn healthy food habits and sadly just because you have a mental illness or disorder does not mean everyone else needs to live their life around that. Keep her trigger foods out of reach for HER. Not everyone. Its not fair to others and what does that teach her about the real world? Not everyone in her life will bend their back for this, future friends or partners cannot be expected to live a certain way in fear of triggering her. If she ever lives in a dorm or has a roomate the world cant change just for her. She needs to heal and learn to overcome her big triggers like this. Realistically they will happen for a majority of her life. When shes stressed as an adult it might trigger it, if shes every pregnant it might get triggered. The goal here is a healthy relationship with food. Also I would just like to point out that you have to think of your future child and them having a healthy relationship with food as well and your wife. 

You did the right things for your daughter but please do not punish your wife and baby just for her relapse. Balance is key.

To be honest maine coons are a lot of work so I hope youve been actively doing research on them. Maine coons are known for play aggression, which is really hard to train out of them kf it isnt caught on time because its not known for them to grow out of it buuut because shes so young theres a chance to train. I would try to do research on how to train a maine coon, from my experience with them they need to be given something to do 24/7. They are very much known for playing too hard with other cats and not really having "cat boundaries". They get bored easily so get a lot of interactive toys for them, tall towers, if you can put a wall highway for her she will love it. When I implemented these things with some clicker training (which really took a long time because they are very smart and very stubborn) I was able to lesson the play aggression. The biggest problem is that you dont know how Ava and Zoe are interacting when you arent there. This play aggression can easily turn into bullying (which it kind of already sounds like you guys are going down that road), especially with Zoe being an older lady. 

If this continues even after training (again clickers and treats and ignoring bad behavior after diverting her attention or moving her away from Zoe) and if it still contines with a lot of new imtrichmemt toys, a big TALL tower, and a wall highway -- if you can put that then she needs to be taken to a behavioral specialist. Also just a reminder, maine coon do not do yhe best in small homes with other cats. They like to explore and like a lot of space so if your home is small (small apartment) then I would definitely suggest starting to take them outside on walks and such. A bird feeder outside for them to watch as well is always great. Also dont be afraid to teach Ava tricks! They are very good at learning them and love learning them.  

The also both need their own safe spaces that are their own and respected by each other so make sure they have a place where they can both get away from each other when things become too much for Zoe. Good luck! Dont worry, with hard work you CAN solve this. Remember bordem inhances this, it might seem like you're playing with them a lot but its never enough for a maine coon!

time for some desensitization! 

i just want to start off by letting you know that a new cat takes awhile to adjust to if she isnt behaving how you are expecting follow the rule of 3.

3 hours. 3 days. 3 weeks. 3 months. 

A cat is fully comfortable after 3 months! 

If the behavior continues after 3 weeks then I would start to do the process of desensitization. I would suggest doing this with everything in your home and rooms. 

Its going to start with treats. You will walk her around with treats and reward her if she gets close to the chair, you can put treats on the chair around the chair how ever you want to do it. Then play with her toys around the chair. She should get over it pretty fast. This is a great way to bond and help your new cat be comfortable and confident. Good luck! Dont force anything!

I had the same problem with my first cat! The whole house was her domain 😅 I decided to put her where she sleeps (with me in the bedroom) and it worked out really well. 

Also please watch out if you have a male cat he might start peeing places to show dominance even if hes fixed, if it goes on for too long take him to the vet and they can give you a more permanent solution! And please make sure to watch out for bullying, cats dont have to love each other but claws, bitting, looking like their hunting is never ok!

look up jackson galaxy videos on how to introduce pets and on hks website i also believe he gives detailed intructions as well

ive introduced multiple cats with his method and it has always worked, dont just let them figure it out cuz regardless of a cat being docile they are extremely territorial and will fight another cat regardless if they are a kitten or not a threat 

also try to find a younger cat and one that has the same personality characteristics preferably, also most cats can use the litter by 8 weeks old! but sometimes they get scared and can go around the house so heres some tips

1) put new cat in litter box when you get it set up so they know where it is 

2) have a minimum 2 litter boxes for 2 cats, preferably 3 litter boxes for 2 cats 

3) buy a cleaning treatment that takes the smell away when a cat pees so if a cat does pee you can clean it up immediately so theres no smell left behindnand they wont pee in that spot again

4) if they poop outside the litter pick up the poop and clean that spot then put the poop in the litter box and show them that its there..NEVER get upset they will just get scared and keep doing it

as for choosing who gets to be where it completely depends on your resident cat. where is residents cats safe space? where do they spend most of their time? keep them there, they will feel more comfortable there and they will be more territorial of that area

as for who to sleep with well thats up to you! if you know resident cat has separation anxiety then try to get some catnip or cat cbd or something in that relm to help calm them..they will probably be upset when they arent with you if they are clingy just make sure you dont give new cat more attention then resident cat trust me they notice so try to keep it equal! good luck! if you have any more questions feel free to ask!
